what: the union of the twelve target compilers' own type enumerations, step A of the node type_vocabulary

markers.x: present in that language's own enumeration
markers.~: present but qualified; the raw field says how
absent from that language's own enumeration

qualified_cells_whose_note_is_prose.raw: WeakReference, WeakMap (class list, not used for presence)
Option is a library enum, absent from TyKind
void is a language keyword, not a dart:core declaration
Never is in dart's type system but is not declared in dart:core
Result is a library enum, absent from TyKind

entries.label: boolean
entries.note: ruby spells it as two classes with one value each

entries.label: integer (fixed-width whole number)
entries.note: python and ruby have no fixed-width integer at all; their whole-number type is arbitrary-precision and sits in the bigint row. typescript has neither: `number` is the double.

cpp.raw: signed char, short, int, long, long long

swift.raw: struct Int, Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, Int128

entries.label: bigint (arbitrary-precision whole number)
entries.note: swift's StaticBigInt only types a literal, it is not a value type a program computes with

entries.label: unsigned integer
entries.note: java has no unsigned type at all

cpp.raw: unsigned char, unsigned short, unsigned int, unsigned long, unsigned long long

swift.raw: struct UInt, UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, UInt128

entries.label: pointer-sized integer
entries.note: the width follows the machine word rather than the source

cpp.raw: size_t is a typedef, not a fundamental type

swift.raw: struct Int is word-sized, but not a separate type

entries.label: complex number
entries.note: named in the CORE's first-pass expectation; the measurement confirms it at 3 of 12

entries.label: rational number
entries.note: exact fractions; only ruby ships one as a core class

entries.label: char / unicode scalar
entries.note: python, typescript, ruby, php and dart have no character type; a one-element string stands in

go.raw: untyped rune in go/types; rune is an alias for int32, not a distinct reflect.Kind

entries.label: string / text
entries.note: java and cpp are the two whose compiler-level enumeration has no text type: java.lang.String is a DECLARED reference and std::string is a library class template

entries.label: byte buffer / raw bytes
entries.note: three languages have byte-oriented strings instead of a separate buffer type

go.raw: []byte is a slice of uint8, not a distinct kind

entries.label: list (growable ordered sequence)
entries.note: java's ArrayList, csharp's List<T>, cpp's std::vector and rust's Vec are library types; none appears in those four compilers' own type enumerations

typescript.raw: ObjectFlags ArrayLiteral, EvolvingArray; Array itself is a lib.d.ts interface

rust.raw: Slice is a borrowed view; Vec is a library type, absent from TyKind

entries.label: fixed-size array
entries.note: length is part of the type

entries.label: slice / view into a sequence
entries.note: borrows storage it does not own

go.raw: a go slice is both the view and the growable list

entries.label: dict (key-to-value map)
entries.note: a verified instrument, yet only 6 of 12 compilers enumerate it; elsewhere it is a library class

php.raw: array (gettype) -- php's one array type IS the hash map

entries.label: set
entries.note: the CORE flags this as a candidate derivation from dict

go.raw: go/types Tuple exists only for call signatures, never as a value type

kotlin.raw: Pair, Triple are stdlib types, not a language form

python.raw: SimpleNamespace; no struct form in the type table

entries.label: class / object with identity
entries.note: go and rust have no class form at all

entries.label: enum / tagged variant
entries.note: java's TypeKind has no enum entry (an enum is a DECLARED class) and csharp's CorElementType has none either (an enum is a VALUETYPE)

php.raw: UnitEnum, BackedEnum -- enums are objects with marker interfaces

swift.raw: struct Range, ClosedRange, PartialRangeFrom, PartialRangeThrough, PartialRangeUpTo

entries.label: iterator / sequence
entries.note: swift's ~40 lazy and adapter sequence types fold here

python.raw: GeneratorType, enumerate, filter, map, reversed, zip

swift.raw: protocol Sequence, IteratorProtocol; struct AnyIterator, AnySequence, LazySequence

typescript.raw: no TypeFlags entry; function types are Object types carrying call signatures

php.raw: Closure is a class; `callable` is a declaration-position type name

swift.raw: function types are structural; the stdlib has no nominal function type

entries.label: closure / coroutine / generator (callable carrying state)
entries.note: rustc gives these four TyKind variants of their own, which is why they earn a row separate from function

php.raw: IS_REFERENCE is a zval tag, not a declarable type

entries.label: weak reference
entries.note: php's WeakReference/WeakMap are core classes, but this measurement does not read presence off php's class list (decision 6), so php is marked qualified

python.raw: weakref is a stdlib module, not a builtin type

php.raw: WeakReference, WeakMap (class list, not used for presence)

dart.raw: final class WeakReference, class Expando, abstract final class Finalizer

entries.label: channel (typed queue between tasks)
entries.note: the CORE's own example of a single-language type that stays in

ruby.raw: Queue, SizedQueue are core classes, but thread queues rather than a type form

entries.label: optional wrapper (adds absence to a type)
entries.note: rust's Option is a library enum with no TyKind of its own; three languages spell optionality as a modifier rather than a type

typescript.raw: modelled as a union with Undefined

rust.raw: Option is a library enum, absent from TyKind

kotlin.raw: T? is a modifier the compiler tracks, not a builtin classifier

entries.label: the absent value's own type (null/nil/None)
entries.note: csharp, rust, kotlin and swift give the absent value no type of its own

typescript.raw: Null and Undefined -- two of them

entries.label: void / unit (no meaningful value)
entries.note: half the set has a real type here and half fakes it with the absent value or with no return at all

python.raw: None doubles as the unit value

go.raw: a function may return nothing; there is no unit type

rust.raw: the empty Tuple is the unit

php.raw: void is a declaration-position type name

dart.raw: void is a language keyword, not a dart:core declaration

entries.label: never / bottom (the type with no values)

php.raw: never is a declaration-position return type

dart.raw: Never is in dart's type system but is not declared in dart:core

entries.label: any / top (every value belongs to it)

typescript.raw: Any and Unknown -- two of them

java.raw: java.lang.Object is a DECLARED reference, not a TypeKind

php.raw: mixed is a declaration-position type name

java.raw: DECLARED covers classes and interfaces alike

entries.label: runtime type object (a value denoting a type)

swift.raw: metatypes T.Type are a language form with no stdlib nominal type

entries.label: error / exception type

go.raw: error is a universe-scope interface, not a BasicKind

dart.raw: class Error, abstract interface class Exception

rust.raw: Result is a library enum, absent from TyKind

swift.raw: struct SIMD2, SIMD3, SIMD4, SIMD8, SIMD16, SIMD32, SIMD64, SIMDMask; protocol SIMD, SIMDScalar
class KeyPath, WritableKeyPath, ReferenceWritableKeyPath, PartialKeyPath, AnyKeyPath

ruby.raw: Module doubles as the mixin form

entries.label: uri
entries.note: the weakest data entry: parsed text that only dart puts in its core

dart.raw: abstract interface class Uri, final class UriData

entries.label: text builder (mutable text accumulator)
entries.note: java's StringBuilder and python's io.StringIO are library types; only dart's core declares one

dart.raw: class StringBuffer, abstract interface class StringSink

entries.label: union type (a value is one of several)

entries.label: wildcard (bounded unknown type argument)
entries.note: java alone gives this a type kind

entries.label: applied generic (a generic with its arguments filled in)

entries.label: type operator (conditional, keyof, indexed access, mapped)

entries.note: rust alone

entries.label: pattern-restricted type (values narrowed by a pattern)
entries.note: rust alone
